title: Neo-Hookean small-on-large wave oracle
purpose: Freeze the material tangent and reference/current direction conventions used to judge wave propagation about a homogeneous prestrained state.

execution.evidence: The analytical dP/dF and acoustic tensor are tested independently. A finite-strain Explicit strip then measures direct longitudinal-wave arrival at zero and ten-percent held prestrain; 40-to-80-cell refinement reduces the arrival-speed error and the fine cases remain within two percent.

observables: Material acoustic tensor Q[i,k] for a reference propagation direction.
Reference and current propagation directions and deformation Jacobian.
acceptance: The analytical tangent matches a centered first-Piola derivative.
At F=I the acoustic eigenvalues recover c_s and c_d.
Equivalent current- and reference-direction declarations return the same physical speeds.
The 80-cell zero- and ten-percent-prestrain arrival speeds differ from the material acoustic-tensor prediction by less than two percent.
The no-fracture relative energy error decreases under 40-to-80-cell refinement.
limitations: The returned modes are bulk waves; a prestrained Rayleigh speed requires a separate surface-wave secular solution.
The two-dimensional implementation follows the current plane-strain constitutive restriction.
Loss of positive definiteness is reported as loss of strong ellipticity, not regularized.
